# Stage 3 replay — microprice in quoting — DOT-USD

**Status**: COMPLETE — PASS (capped). Generated by `scripts/replay_microprice.py`
on real DOT `book_change` data (VPS, 2026-05-22).

Real `PricingEngine.compute_target_price` run twice per `book_change` snapshot
(use_microprice False vs True). Measures the per-quote perturbation. No PnL
claim — that is the live A/B (Phase 3 cont.).

Journals: `mm_DOT-USD_20260515_162308.jsonl` (+ `.3` rotation).

## Result (capped engine, MM_MICROPRICE_CAP_BPS=10)

- book_change snapshots used: **17,155** (errors: 0)
- snapshots with non-zero (micro−mid): 6,845 (39.9% of used)

- bid/ask perturbation identical (additive recenter): **OK** (0 mismatches)

## VERDICT: **PASS** — cleared for DOT iter002 live A/B

The recentering is correctly signed, symmetric, bounded, and exception-free on
real book data.

## Why the cap was added (the replay earned its keep)

The **uncapped** first run showed an identical distribution on calm/normal
books (overall p99 5.33 bps, calm p99 2.34 bps) but a **75.35 bps max** on
wide/dislocated books (spread > 20 bps, ~5% of snapshots). Microprice is
known-unreliable on dislocated/dust-quote books — the same mechanism behind
the Stage 3 *TradFi wrong-sign* finding. Every other signal in the bot is
capped (funding 8 bps, OFI 3 bps planned); microprice was not.

`MM_MICROPRICE_CAP_BPS` (default 10) was added. Re-running the capped engine:
**max |shift| 75.35 → 9.84 bps**, with the calm/normal distribution untouched
(p99 unchanged). The cap clips only the dangerous tail.

This is exactly the integration-sanity issue the replay gate exists to catch —
not a calibration-vs-impl gap (microprice has no calibration model), but an
unbounded-magnitude tail on adversarial book states.
